notes: Verbless in principle (LLPSI cap. II); the action runs on the G02 whitelist of 3rd-person present verbs (говори́т, кричи́т, пла́чет, сиди́т, стои́т, лежи́т, смо́трит, спит, и́щет, зна́ет, спра́шивает, отвеча́ет), each glossed at first use and declared incidental. No accusative (G04): nobody looks *at* anything; смо́трит stands alone.
In this household Шарик sleeps on straw in the yard (во дворе́), not under the table; the cover brief shows him at the open door.

Planted: «Царь не зна́ет» (Дед, comic here) is the Глава 29 theme «the Tsar does not know»; Ivan cannot read «Росси́я» on Nastya's slate (Главы 5–6); Pyotr makes Ivan mend the slate (Глава 3 opens with it).

Pensum C has no «Почему́?» item although the checker asks for one from Глава 2: почему́ is a Глава 3 lexeme (Codex: using it here would be unlicensed); the «why» question is «Где доска́? Кто винова́т?».

Warnings left, with reasons: gloss density 4.1/100 (every whitelisted verb is glossed at its first use, as the brief requires); prior coverage 46.6% (bootstrap floor 60%): Глава 2 introduces the household, the pronouns and the possessives at once (35 planned lexemes, 23 of them known to the owner per plan/baseline.json), and its incidental verbs count as aided, not prior; Pensum A a10 recalls G01 one chapter back, as plan/recall.json prescribes for Глава 2 (the checker expects 2–6); new-cluster in 6 sentences (household introductions); stress-unverified by design.
Words used once with a gloss in their segment (Часть 1 has no open slots, so they are not lexemes): полови́на (= ½), соло́ма, тесноте́/оби́де (proverb), двена́дцать, бу́квы (Глава 5 lexeme).

cover.alt: The Sokolov family at supper in their izba: the father at the head of the table under the icons and a small portrait of the Tsar, the mother standing with a ladle, the grandfather by the stove, the elder son and his wife with two small children, Ivan, and Nastya holding half of a broken slate; the dog looks in at the open door.
cover.art_brief: Interior of a Ryazan peasant izba, late April 1913, evening light from one small window and a lamp. A long plank table with a round loaf. At its head Pyotr Matveyevich (about 55, grey-brown beard, belted shirt) under the icon corner with a small framed portrait of Nicholas II. Marya Stepanovna (about 50, dark kerchief) standing with a wooden ladle. Ded Matvei (70, white beard) sitting by the big white stove. Fyodor (27, broad, dark beard) and Darya (25, kerchief) with Misha (6) and Liza (4) on the bench. Ivan (19, tall, fair, beardless). Nastya (12, braid, kerchief) holding up half of a wooden-framed school slate, mouth open. Shaggy grey-and-white mongrel Sharik peeking in at the open door from the yard. No text.

words_with_history.title: Слова́ с исто́рией
text: Ма́рья Степа́новна говори́т «семья́»: вот стол, вот хлеб, вот де́ти.
Пётр Матве́евич говори́т «двор»: двор — э́то семья́, хлеб и по́ле.
А Ша́рик лежи́т во дворе́: э́то его́ двор.
words_with_history.note_en: A двор was also a peasant household: its head, here Pyotr, answered for it and spoke at the village assembly (сход). Семья́ is the people at the table. The proverb: 'in a family even the porridge is thicker'.

grammar.title: Стол — столы́, доска́ — до́ски
grammar.rule: стол → столы́, шко́ла → шко́лы · доска́ → до́ски, дере́вня → дере́вни · по́ле → поля́ · брат → бра́тья, ребёнок → де́ти · ста́рые, больши́е
grammar.note_en: Regular plurals: -ы, but -и after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ and usually for nouns in -я/-ь (до́ски, дере́вни); neuter -о/-е usually gives -а/-я (поля́). Some masculine nouns take stressed -а (города́); some plurals are irregular (бра́тья, сыновья́, де́ти; мать and дочь change more). Adjectives: -ые, or -ие after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ (больши́е, ма́ленькие). Stress often moves (доска́ → до́ски). его́, её, их never change.
